title: An Effective Machine Learning Frame for Materials Discovery Structured by a Chemical Concept
experiments_summary: The study implements a six-step workflow: (1) Training set preparation using 57 known metal superhydride prototypes, expanded via s-d border metal substitutions. (2) Feature engineering to represent metal lattices and their interstitial electron localization (quasi-atom) properties. (3) ML model training to learn the relationship between metal lattice characteristics and thermodynamic stability, achieving MAE of 11 meV/atom and R² = 0.95. (4) Metal lattice candidate preparation, generating nearly 8,000 hypothetical lattices. (5) Metal lattice screening using the trained ML model to select ~1,400 promising candidates exhibiting strong template effects (significant electron localization at interstitial sites). (6) High-throughput DFT-based computational screening of metal superhydrides derived from the selected metal lattices, varying metal-to-hydrogen ratios including non-integer stoichiometries, with unit cells ranging from 50 to 94 atoms. Structural searches placed hydrogen atoms into interstitial sites of pre-selected metal lattices rather than simultaneously optimizing both metal and hydrogen positions. Thermodynamic stability was assessed via DFT, with zero-point energy (ZPE) and finite-temperature corrections applied. Dynamical stability was confirmed through phonon spectrum calculations. Superconducting transition temperatures were estimated using descriptors including three-dimensional electronic connectivity, hydrogen content, and hydrogen contribution to the electronic density of states at the Fermi level. Electron-phonon coupling calculations were explicitly performed for Pm3n-Ca8H46 at 200 GPa to validate the workflow, yielding the logarithmic average phonon frequency, electron-phonon coupling constant (λ), and Tc estimates under varying Coulomb pseudopotential (µ* = 0.1–0.13).
